intro.p1: Geist is our primary typeface, chosen for its clarity and the quiet confidence it brings to everything Rectio says.
intro.p2: It includes a wide range of weights and styles to maximize the function and flexibility of our system.

system.heading: Our type system
system.p1: Geist and Space Grotesk are open-source typefaces chosen for Rectio. Utilitarian yet characterful, together they balance expression with function across all brand expressions.
system.p2: Their shapes are sleek and modern while retaining some unique quirks and characteristics:

families.label: Primary Font Family
families.text: Geist is a modern, neutral sans-serif typeface designed for clarity and readability across digital interfaces. Its clean forms, balanced proportions, and broad range of weights give Rectio a precise, contemporary, and highly adaptable typographic system.

families.label: Secondary Font Family
families.text: Space Grotesk is a geometric sans-serif designed for clarity with a distinctive character. Its open forms and balanced proportions make it ideal for supporting headlines, highlights, and expressive brand communication.

typesetting.heading: Typesetting
typesetting.p1: Typesetting is the process of selecting and arranging our fonts with consistent sizing, spacing, and alignment principles.
typesetting.p2: This section outlines our standard typographic hierarchy and demonstrates use cases for each member of our font family.

hierarchy.title: Extra Large Headline
text: Extra large headlines don’t appear in all standard documents, appearing in places like presentation covers, divider slides or physical signage.
Extra large headlines are set in Space Grotesk Light.

hierarchy.title: Headline
text: Space Grotesk Medium is used for all external-facing headlines, set in title case for everyday documents or sentence case for comms.

hierarchy.title: Subhead
text: Space Grotesk Medium is used for all standard subheads, set in title case for everyday documents or sentence case for comms.

hierarchy.title: Body copy
text: Use Geist Regular for body text, captions, and other detailed info.

scale.title: Type scale
scale.text: Every level of our hierarchy maps to a fixed size and line height. Pick the closest level rather than setting a custom size, so layouts stay consistent across documents and screens.

tracking.title: Tracking
tracking.text: All of our text styles are set with 0 tracking. Geist and Space Grotesk are spaced for both display and text sizes, so leave letter-spacing at its default.

color.heading: Standard Color
color.p1: When applying color to type, keep it simple and functional. Our standard approach is to use Black or White across all levels. Limit yourself to a single type color per layout.
color.p2: Always choose your type color to maximize contrast and legibility. For example, don’t use Pampas text over a Pampas background. Here are some approved type and background combinations:

roles.label: Headline
roles.text: On light backgrounds, set all text in Black.

roles.label: Subhead
roles.text: Limit yourself to one text color per layout.

roles.label: Body Copy
roles.text: Color use should match across headline, subheads, and body copy to help keep our layouts streamlined and clean.

padding.heading: Padding
padding.p1: As our type sizes shift between applications, the vertical padding should scale.
padding.p2: The minimum space following any headline should be 75% of the headline’s cap height. The minimum space following a subhead or body paragraph is equal to 100% of the subhead body copy’s cap height.
padding.noteText: This is a good rule of thumb for most applications. In layouts with limited space, padding between type can be condensed.

leading.heading: Leading
leading.text: Use this formula to determine leading values based on type size. Leading ratios (L) are predetermined for each level of type hierarchy according to the table here. For example, if your subhead size is 100pts, your leading is 100 x 1.2, or 120pts.

formula.aria: Type size times leading ratio equals leading
formula.noteText: Some extra large headlines may require tighter leading. Always begin with a 1.0 ratio and reduce incrementally, if desired.

capitalization.heading: Capitalization
capitalization.p1: Headlines and subheads in external communications are set using sentence case capitalization. This keeps our content colloquial, casual, and consistent. Punctuation may be included where necessary for tone and grammar.
capitalization.p2: Please note that this differs from our rule for internal documents (like PowerPoint presentations or Word documents) which use title case capitalization for presentation titles, page headers, or section names.
capitalization.sentenceNote: Use sentence case capitalization when speaking externally to customers.
capitalization.titleNote: Use title case capitalization for routine internal documents.
capitalization.capsNote: Don’t use all-caps headlines for any document type or audience.
capitalization.altSentence: headlines are set in sentence case
capitalization.altTitle: Internal Headlines Are Set in Title Case
capitalization.altCaps: WE NEVER SET HEADLINES IN ALL-CAPS

lineLengths.heading: Line Lengths
lineLengths.p1: For best legibility, lines of text shouldn’t be too long or short. Headlines should have between 4 and 15 characters per line, and paragraphs should have between 40 and 70 characters per line.
lineLengths.p2: If the line length of a body paragraph becomes too long, divide the text into columns. Remember, spaces and punctuation count as characters.
